fix(explain): report the OpenCode agent permission that sync writes

`explain` now reports the permission keys that `sync` writes for an OpenCode agent's `tools`, such as `read` and `bash`, instead of listing them as unsupported.

The OpenCode adapter had no agent translation, so it fell through to a table with no portable names. It now reuses the same rule translation the permission writer uses, so there is no second table.

Kilo already had this translation, so it needed no change. The new test covers both: it syncs an agent with `tools: [Read, Bash]` and checks that each row `explain` reports is a permission key in the synced file.

Checks run: the explain tests, the opencode and adapters packages, `go vet`, and `sync --check`.

Closes #3425

Templates: show and require maxacpower for curtailers

Follow-up to #32451, fixes https://github.com/evcc-io/evcc/pull/35638#issuecomment-6845766216

Curtailer templates (e.g. sungrow-hybrid) need `maxacpower` to convert percent into watts. The default param restricts it to `usages: ["pv"]`, which hides it in the curtailer modal (`DeviceModalBase` filters by device type) and skips the required check (curtailers render with empty usage).

- `defaults.yaml`: `maxacpower` usages `["pv", "curtailer"]`
- `RenderResult`: without a usage param, match param usages against the class name
- TS `TemplateParamUsage`: add `curtailer`
- template tests fail when a param's usages can never match the template's usages or class; the usage filter e2e test moves to a dedicated mock template
- Atmoce: make `maxacpower` required

Unset `maxacpower` renders 0 W limits, i.e. any curtailment below 100% would switch the inverter off. Existing Atmoce pv configurations without `maxacpower` will fail with ``missing required `maxacpower` `` until it is set.

Issue agent: fix unbalanced parenthesis in claude_args

The \`claude_args\` expression of the reusable issue agent workflow lost its closing parenthesis in evcc-io/evcc@2c66df3dd, when the triage branch was wrapped in \`format()\`. GitHub rejects the workflow file with \`Unexpected end of expression: ')'\`, so every run of triage, \`/analyze\` and \`/fix\` fails before any job starts, e.g. https://github.com/evcc-io/evcc/actions/runs/43416444374.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(pi): fix pi binary not found in the install shell

I'm trying `coi` (v0.16.0) for the first time, and I wanted an image with `pi` only, so I've tried that and `coi build`:

```
[container.build]
agents = ["pi"]

[tool]
name = "pi"
```

I've got this error:

```
[...]
Verifying managed Pi 1.5.2
Activating managed Pi 1.5.2
Managed Pi install complete

Pi was installed successfully.

Update Pi later with: pi update
Pi was installed, but your shell is not using that install yet.
Restart your shell or run:

  export PATH="/home/code/.pi/agent/bin:$PATH"

Then run: pi
[coi] ERROR: pi binary not found after installation.
Cleaning up build container...
Error: configure-session: build failed: build script failed: exit status 1
```

Digging a bit, I think it's because the [image build script](https://github.com/coipond/coi/blob/e3021dd452b91586bbcd6f188299b1afd39656e6/internal/image/build.sh#L827) expects `pi` would be in `$PATH` in a new shell (via `su -`):

```
PI_BIN="$(su - "$CODE_USER" -c 'which pi' 2>/dev/null || true)"
```

But it seems that the pi installer script (`https://pi.dev/install.sh` - can't find sources on github) does not add any `PATH=...` line to shell profile, or only does it after confirmation in an interactive `tty`.  Hence the proposed change: look for `pi` directly where the installer will have installed it.

I've been able to finish my `coi build` with this change:

```
[...]
Pi was installed, but your shell is not using that install yet.
Restart your shell or run:

  export PATH="/home/code/.pi/agent/bin:$PATH"

Then run: pi
[coi] pi 1.5.2
[coi] Installing dummy (test stub for testing)...
[coi] dummy Dummy CLI 1.0.0 (test stub)
[coi] Installing Docker...
[...]
```

diff --git a/internal/image/build.sh b/internal/image/build.sh
index 3ca7a04f..7d6d59a5 100644
--- a/internal/image/build.sh
+++ b/internal/image/build.sh
@@ -829,11 +829,11 @@ install_pi() {
         sleep 10
     done
 
-    # Ensure pi is available system-wide for non-login/non-interactive shells
-    local PI_BIN
-    PI_BIN="$(su - "$CODE_USER" -c 'which pi' 2>/dev/null || true)"
-    if [[ -z "$PI_BIN" ]]; then
-        log "ERROR: pi binary not found after installation."
+    # Ensure pi is available system-wide
+    local PI_BIN="/home/$CODE_USER/.pi/agent/bin/pi"
+    if [[ ! -x "$PI_BIN" ]]; then
+        log "ERROR: pi binary not found at $PI_BIN after installation."
+        log "Installation may have failed or installed to an unexpected location."
         exit 1
     fi
     ln -sf "$PI_BIN" /usr/local/bin/pi

fix(collectors): read Intel xe GPU package temperature from labelled hwmon channels

## Description

Intel Arc GPUs on the `xe` driver reported `temperature_celsius: null`. `getIntelGPUTemp` read only `hwmon*/temp1_input` under the GPU's PCI device. The `xe` driver on Battlemage has no `temp1_input`. It exposes the package temperature as `temp2_input` (label `pkg`) and the VRAM temperature as `temp3_input` (label `vram`).

This PR implements the CodeRabbit Coding Plan on #345. `getIntelGPUTemp` now does this:

- It enumerates every PCI-scoped hwmon `temp*_input` channel in numeric order (`hwmon2` before `hwmon10`, and `temp2` before `temp10`).
- It prefers the channel labelled `pkg` or `package` (case-insensitive, trimmed).
- Otherwise it uses the first usable channel that is not labelled VRAM.
- It never fills `temperature_celsius` from a VRAM channel.

The value rules, the null-versus-zero contract and all consumers are unchanged. VRAM temperature and GPU fan attribution are tracked separately in #347.

## Hardware Configuration (if applicable)

- **CPU:** Intel Core Ultra 5 245K (Arrow Lake-S), MSI PRO B860M-A WIFI
- **Disk Controller:** Not relevant to this change
- **GPU:** Intel Arc Pro B70 / Battlemage G31 (`0000:04:00.0`, `xe`) and Intel Arrow Lake-S iGPU (`0000:00:02.0`, `i915`)
- **UPS:** Not relevant to this change
- **Network:** Not relevant to this change
- **Other:** The `xe` hwmon (`hwmon6`) exposes `temp2_input`/`temp2_label=pkg` and `temp3_input`/`temp3_label=vram`, and no `temp1_input`
- **Unraid Version:** 7.4.0 (kernel 6.18.60-Unraid), agent 2026.11.05 installed

## Changes Made

- `daemon/services/collectors/gpu.go`:
  - `getIntelGPUTemp` globs `hwmon/hwmon*/temp*_input` under the PCI device and sorts the paths numerically with the new helper `sortHwmonTempInputs`.
  - It reads each `tempN_label` through the existing `readTrimmed`, and selects `pkg`/`package` first, then the first usable channel without a `vram` label.
  - Unreadable, unparseable, NaN and infinite values are still skipped. A measured zero is still accepted. The function comment is updated.
- `daemon/services/collectors/gpu_measurements_test.go`: new table-driven `TestIntelTemperatureChannelSelection` with 11 cases:
  - the `xe` layout, unlabelled `temp1` (legacy), a padded mixed-case `Package` label
  - NaN and garbled package values that fall back to a non-VRAM channel
  - `vram` only and `vram_ch_0` only (both null)
  - `temp2` before `temp10`, and `hwmon2` before `hwmon10`
  - a measured-zero package value, and a `pkg` channel on another PCI device that is not used
- `daemon/services/collectors/gpu_collection_measurements_test.go`: new `TestCollectSingleIntelGPUTemperatureChannels`, which runs the full single-GPU collection for two layouts:
  - the B70 layout: temperature 46
  - VRAM only: temperature null

  CPU temperature stays separate in both.
- `docs/api/rest-api.md`: a short note about where the Intel GPU temperature comes from. VRAM is not reported in `temperature_celsius`.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: added a `### Fixed` entry under `[Unreleased]`.

No DTO, Swagger, Prometheus, MQTT, `lspci` or `intel_gpu_top` changes.

The new tests fail against `main`'s `gpu.go`, which shows that they reproduce the bug. The fix makes them pass. The legacy cases (unlabelled `temp1`, VRAM only, another device's `pkg`) already passed on `main`; they are kept as contract guards.

On an Intel Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage G31, `xe`, kernel 6.18.60), the GPU temperature was `null` because the driver has no `temp1_input`.

**Fix Implemented:**

The agent selects the hwmon channel by label (`pkg`/`package`). If no channel has that label, it uses the first channel without a `vram` label, in numeric order.

## **Tested On:**

Unraid 7.4.0 with an Intel Arc Pro B70 (`xe`) and an Arrow Lake iGPU (`i915`, which has no hwmon temperature).

Closes #67

## Root causes

**'down keeps the DB unknown' (CI run 42494916942).** The controller caches scanner probe results for one minute, keyed by URL and CA. httptest TLS servers all use the same certificate and the OS reuses ephemeral ports, so a healthy server from an earlier spec left a cached result under the same key as a later, closed server. The spec then saw VulnerabilityDBReady True for 10 s instead of Unknown (the CI log shows exactly that). Fix: the suite keeps the target reconciler and `newFakeTrivy` resets its probe cache. Production behaviour is unchanged.

**First spec 'renders a hardened CronJob' on suite startup.** No failing CI log is left and I could not reproduce it locally (see below). The first spec was the only one paying for informers the controllers start lazily on first Get (Namespace, ConfigMap, Secret, Pod, CronJob, Job) and could reconcile against a fixture target the manager cache had not yet seen as Ready, all inside the 10 s Eventually. BeforeSuite now waits for cache sync, starts those informers, and waits until the manager client sees the fixture target Ready. This is a hardening of the startup race, not a proven fix.

The earlier flake (VulnerabilityException event read once) was already fixed by #79. I scanned the other controller specs for single reads of asynchronous state; the remaining ones (`Expect(mirrorReady(x)())` after a prior Eventually, one absence check in vulngate_test.go) are not clearly racy, so I left them.

**TestGateJavaDB and other internal/sync gate specs (seen once in a full `make test`).** The fake sidecar wrote `out/<hex>.exit` with `os.WriteFile`, which creates the file empty before writing. The client polls that file every few ms, so under load it could read an empty exit file and report `ScanFailed: scanner exited with an error`. The real sidecar script writes a tmp file and renames it (`internal/syncspec/gate.go`); the fake now does the same. It hit more than TestGateJavaDB: TestGateException, TestGateReferrers, TestGateMultiArch, TestGateUnknownPlatformLabel and TestRescan failed the same way.

## Testing

- Reproduction of the scanner flake: a temporary spec (not committed) creates a healthy fake, starts a second fake, closes the first and probes its URL. Before: fails with True vs Unknown. After: passes.
- Repeat runs (separate suite processes, parallel under load, fresh BeforeSuite each time):
  - 'Scanner readiness': 40/40 before, 40/40 after. The collision is rare (needs one reused port within a minute), so only the reproduction above is conclusive.
  - 'renders a hardened CronJob': 40/40 before, 40/40 after, also 40/40 before with 16 busy loops added. I could not trigger the startup failure.
- internal/sync, 12 processes in parallel, 10 passes of the whole package each: 9 of 12 processes failed before (20 failing specs, all through the empty exit file), 0 of 12 after. `TestGateJavaDB -count=50` alone and `-race -count=100` never failed, so it only shows under load.
- `make manifests generate fmt vet lint test` passes (0 lint issues, controller suite ok).

## Docs

No user-visible effect; test-only change.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(e2e): use helm --wait=legacy to avoid kstatus watcher panic

Closes #83

## Changes

- e2e suite, mirror and gate-infra helm calls and `make helm-deploy` use `--wait=legacy` (Helm 3 wait logic) instead of the kstatus watcher.
- `docs/install.md`: short note with the workaround for users who hit the panic.
- Helm pin stays at v4.1.4: no released Helm contains a fix (see below), and Renovate is not configured for it (no renovate config, only dependabot for actions/gomod).

Upstream evidence:
- The panic site is `newStatusCheckTaskFunc` in fluxcd/cli-utils `object_status_reporter.go`: a timer task sends on `eventCh` after the informer goroutine closed it.
- Helm v4.1.4 pulls cli-utils v0.37.2-flux.1; v4.3.1 and v4.3.2 pull v1.2.2; Helm main pulls v1.4.0.
- In cli-utils v1.2.2 and v1.4.0 the task still sends unconditionally (`eventCh <- ...` at lines 937 and 949). The only related change, 376a386 "opt-in async watcher status computation", waits for in-flight work before `close(eventCh)` but is opt-in and does not cover the timer task.
- No open issue found in helm/helm or fluxcd/cli-utils for this panic.

## Testing

- `go vet -tags e2e ./test/e2e/` passes.
- `helm upgrade --help` on v4.1.4 lists `--wait` values `watcher`, `hookOnly`, `legacy`.
- Full e2e not run locally; CI e2e on this PR exercises the legacy wait.

## Docs

`docs/install.md` troubleshooting note. No change to `docs/features.md` (no user-visible feature change).

ci(scripts): run the pinned Vale, not whichever is on PATH

Closes #3763

`scripts/vale.sh` used any `vale` on `PATH`. A newer binary skips the `Vale.Spelling` errors the pinned image reports, so the pre-push hook passed and CI failed.

The binary is now used only when its version matches the pin. Otherwise the script runs the pinned image through Docker. With a different version and no Docker it exits 1 and names both versions; with neither it says what to install.

`scripts/test-vale-script.sh` stubs `vale` and `docker` and covers those cases. It runs in the `changes` job next to the pin check. `CONTRIBUTING.md` describes the new behaviour.

Independent of the gate change that makes `style` required. This only stops the local and CI results diverging.

Stacked on #3760: the pre-push Vale run fails on main's existing prose errors until that merges, so this branch carries its commit underneath. Merge #3760 first and the diff here shrinks to one commit.

diff --git a/scripts/test-vale-script.sh b/scripts/test-vale-script.sh
new file mode 100755
index 000000000..ecda24890
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/test-vale-script.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,60 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# scripts/vale.sh has to run the Vale version CI runs. A newer binary on PATH
+# misses errors the pinned one reports, so the hook passes and CI fails. Stub
+# `vale` and `docker` on a private PATH and check the four ways it can go.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+root=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
+pinned=$(grep -Eo 'jdkato/vale:v[0-9.]+' "$root/scripts/vale.sh" | head -n1 | sed 's/.*:v//')
+
+failed=0
+fail() {
+  echo "FAIL: $1"
+  failed=1
+}
+
+work=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
+
+# stubs <vale-version|-> <docker yes|no>: a fresh bin dir with only what's asked.
+stubs() {
+  local bin="$work/bin"
+  rm -rf "$bin" && mkdir -p "$bin"
+  for tool in bash dirname id pwd sed grep head cut tr; do
+    ln -s "$(command -v $tool)" "$bin/$tool"
+  done
+  # shellcheck disable=SC2016
+  if [ "$1" != - ]; then
+    printf '#!/bin/sh\nif [ "$1" = --version ]; then echo "vale version %s"; else echo "ran-binary $*"; fi\n' "$1" >"$bin/vale"
+    chmod +x "$bin/vale"
+  fi
+  if [ "$2" = yes ]; then
+    printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "ran-docker $*"\n' >"$bin/docker"
+    chmod +x "$bin/docker"
+  fi
+  echo "$bin"
+}
+
+has() { printf '%s' "$1" | grep -Eq -- "$2"; }
+run() { PATH="$1" /usr/bin/env bash "$root/scripts/vale.sh" x.md 2>&1 || echo "exit=$?"; }
+
+out=$(run "$(stubs "$pinned" yes)")
+case "$out" in *ran-binary*) ;; *) fail "a vale at the pinned version should run: $out" ;; esac
+
+out=$(run "$(stubs 9.9.9 yes)")
+case "$out" in *ran-docker*"jdkato/vale:v$pinned@sha256:"*) ;; *) fail "another version with Docker should run the pinned image: $out" ;; esac
+
+out=$(run "$(stubs 9.9.9 no)")
+if ! { has "$out" "exit=[1-9]" && has "$out" "9.9.9" && has "$out" "$pinned"; }; then
+  fail "another version without Docker should fail naming both versions: $out"
+fi
+
+out=$(run "$(stubs - yes)")
+case "$out" in *ran-docker*) ;; *) fail "no vale with Docker should run the pinned image: $out" ;; esac
+
+out=$(run "$(stubs - no)")
+if ! { has "$out" "exit=127" && has "$out" "Docker"; }; then
+  fail "neither should fail and say what to install: $out"
+fi
+
+exit "$failed"

@@ -1,8 +1,8 @@

+# Runs Vale at the version CI runs: the binary on PATH when it is that version
+# (the CI job runs inside the pinned image below, where it is), otherwise the
+# same image through Docker. A different version on PATH is never used.
+# rules/markdown.md, "Running Vale", has the reasoning.
 set -euo pipefail
 
 cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.."
@@ -12,12 +12,24 @@ cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.."
 # renovate: datasource=docker depName=jdkato/vale
 VALE_IMAGE=jdkato/vale:v3.17.1@sha256:7dba3c9104ba366f172d119022c4ec53a005f7d14dc1b80e285421a3f0b71657
 
-if command -v vale >/dev/null 2>&1; then
-  exec vale "$@"
-fi
+pinned_version=${VALE_IMAGE#*:v}
+pinned_version=${pinned_version%%@*}
 
-if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
-  echo "Vale needs either a vale binary on PATH or Docker to run $VALE_IMAGE" >&2
+# The binary only counts at the pinned version. A newer one skips the
+# Vale.Spelling errors the pinned one reports, so the hook would pass and CI

+  if [ "$found" = "$pinned_version" ]; then
+    exec vale "$@"
+  fi
+  if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "vale on PATH is ${found:-of unknown version}, CI runs $pinned_version." >&2

+  fi
+elif ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  echo "Vale needs either vale $pinned_version on PATH or Docker to run $VALE_IMAGE" >&2
   exit 127
 fi
